question: Everything the earlier waves left alone: Access Configuration, HR, Tasks, Calendar, CRM, Profiling.
environment: dev (oqermaidggvanahumjmj); one read-only check against prod (ubspbukgcxmzegnomlgi)

findings.title: An anonymous stranger can rewrite the permission cascade
findings.purpose: 609 rules of the form parent_key -> child_key deciding which grants imply which other grants

measured_prod.note: READ-ONLY check of RLS state, grants and row count. No write of any kind was made against prod.

proof.method: PostgREST calls with only the publishable anon key — no login, no session, no account
proof.cleanup: DELETE http=204, verified gone; dev is clean

escalation_mechanism.trigger: BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF module_grants on permission_overrides AND access_profiles -> trg_materialize_grant_cascade
escalation_mechanism.function: materialize_grant_cascade(grants jsonb) reads access_cascade_edges and copies the parent grant's value onto any child key absent from the blob
escalation_mechanism.attack: Insert one edge from a grant everybody holds to a grant you want, then wait. The next legitimate admin profile-apply or access edit materializes the planted grant onto that user's row. The audit trail shows an admin doing their job.
escalation_mechanism.what_slows_it: Direct writes to permission_overrides still require current_user_can_manage_admin_users(), so this is staged rather than one-shot.
escalation_mechanism.second_vector: anon holds TRUNCATE. Emptying the table grants nothing but silently strips every cascade rule from all future grant applications — users lose tabs and nobody connects it to a lookup table.

fix: alter table public.access_cascade_edges enable row level security;
revoke all on public.access_cascade_edges from anon, authenticated;
findings.fix_note: Reads happen inside a SECURITY DEFINER function, so nothing legitimate needs direct table access. Prod needs the same and prod needs explicit permission.
findings.why_missed_before: Wave 0 swept the business tables. This is infrastructure, in a corner nothing exercises.

findings.title: The entire HR module is a mockup
findings.framing: Not a defect in the sense this document usually means — nothing is computed wrongly because nothing is computed. It is a demo shell mounted in a production navigation tree and should be behind a flag.
findings.extends: Q7 (Wave 2) found the payslip was mock; it is the whole module.

findings.title: Calendar reminders are stored and never delivered
Built, mounted, never exercised
findings.headline: The modules outside the money spine are not broken, they are untouched — which is also why nobody found the bugs in them, including T1.

findings.title: The KPI tables barely exist
findings.links_to: P7 — the engine scores an empty result set as perfect. This is the other half: there is almost no stored data for it to work from, which is exactly the condition that produces the false 100s.

findings.title: Access Configuration is internally consistent
verified: No orphan grant keys: every one of the 317 distinct doors granted to at least one user is declared in accessSchema.ts / permissionsConfig.ts.

The RBAC backup tables fail closed: _rbac_backup_access_profiles (56), _rbac_backup_permission_overrides (60) and permission_grant_archive (56) all have RLS ENABLED with ZERO policies — deny-all for everyone but service role. That is the exact treatment access_cascade_edges should have had.
findings.self_correction: My first extraction reported 21 orphan doors. That was a regex missing the parent-module helper in accessSchema.ts, not a real gap — all 21 are declared. Recorded so the number is not repeated as fact.

verdict: Wave 5 was supposed to be the quiet one. Instead it found the only unauthenticated write to production in the whole campaign, in a two-column lookup table nobody thought of as data. T1 has presumably been open since migration 198 shipped, because nothing anyone did would ever have surfaced it.
recommended_order: T1 immediately on dev, and on prod with explicit go-ahead — it is two statements and it is live now
T4 and T5 are coverage gaps, not defects
